1.explanation: These files implement the FluidTextInput component, its style, documentation and tests. FluidTextInput.js is where skeleton prop logic must be handled and import the SkeletonPlaceholder or render skeleton markup. index.js must export any new FluidTextInput.Skeleton variant. The SCSS file needs the skeleton selectors (background, border and bar heights/spacing). The stories file needs a skeleton story to preview. The unit test must verify that skeleton renders properly and the e2e test must cover the loading state. All these modules require updates to add and validate the new skeleton functionality for FluidTextInput.
1.bug_scenario:
When a FluidTextInput is rendered with skeleton={true}, nothing special happens – the normal input shows or the component simply ignores the skeleton prop. The design spec calls for a gray “skeleton” placeholder (background filled, no active border, with one or two bar elements indicating loading content) but FluidTextInput has no built-in skeleton state. In the reproduction code you import <FluidTextInput skeleton={true} />, but you see no skeleton bars in the picture.

The screenshots in the report show a background block with subtle border-bottom and one or two lighter gray bars (text placeholder) spaced at 8px or 12px/16px from the edges. This visual behavior must be added to FluidTextInput.

2.explanation:
• FluidTextInput.js – this is the main component.  It needs to check for the skeleton prop and render the new FluidTextInput.Skeleton component (or a SkeletonPlaceholder/SkeletonText markup) instead of the ordinary input.

• index.js – the entry point for the FluidTextInput export.  It must also export the new FluidTextInput.Skeleton (so users can import it directly if they want), and re-export the updated default.

• FluidTextInput.Skeleton.js – a new file that mirrors the pattern in TextInput.Skeleton.js (and other .Skeleton variants) and actually renders the placeholder bars with the proper classnames and styling.

• FluidTextInput.stories.js – update the Storybook stories to include a “with skeleton” example, so designers and engineers can preview the new loading state.

• __tests__/FluidTextInput-test.js – update or add tests to assert that when skeleton=true, the component renders the skeleton markup (e.g. correct .bx--skeleton–fluid classes, no input element, two placeholder bars, etc.).
2.bug_scenario:
When you mount a FluidTextInput with the skeleton prop set to true (e.g.

    <FluidTextInput
      id="test-input"
      labelText="Test Input"
      skeleton={true}
    />

) nothing changes visually — the input never goes into a “loading” or placeholder state.  The spec image shows that a fluid text input should render with a light gray background, a single skeleton‐colored bottom border and a pair of gray bar placeholders (one short, one long) to indicate loading text.  Because no .Skeleton implementation exists for FluidTextInput, the component never renders a placeholder UI when skeleton=true.
